newsitem.title: USA: Geron shares tumble as lock-up period ends.
newsitem.headline: Geron shares tumble as lock-up period ends.

text.p: Geron Corp shares fell sharply Monday as investors took profits following the expiration yesterday of the 180-day lock-up period following the biotechnology company's initial public offering.
Chief Financial Officer David Greenwood confirmed the reason for the decline and said Geron management was not among the sellers.
In early afternoon Nasdaq trade, Geron shares were off almost 20 percent, down 2-7/8 to 11-7/8. Over 313,000 shares had been traded, almost five times the average daily volume.
Geron went public last summer with a two million share offering priced at $8 per share.
J.P. Morgan was the lead underwriter.
